one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-11-12. TI reports Q3 on Oct 21 [19], a read-across for analog/industrial demand. ST reports Q3 on Oct 29 [18] with its Q4 guide. Management already promised Q4 revenue 'above $4 billion' and Q3 of $3.70B with 37% GM [2], so the bar is high and explicit. ST's last two guide disappointments moved the stock -12% (Oct 2025) and -15% (Jul 2026) [6,11]. Offsetting that, the stock is already down ~16% from last week's $59.29 high and 39% from the June peak, and short interest is only 2.44% [14], so a clean beat-and-confirm could bounce it. I put the median slightly below spot ($49.2) for my skeptic view that the Q4 bar is hard to clear. I use a 0.18 one-month log sigma: 61% annual realized vol / 3.5 = 17.4%, plus a little for the earnings event. The result is roughly symmetric, about 48% to finish above $49.57.

fair_value.method: Blend of 17x NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon (~$2.68, model-derived, ~20% below consensus) = $45.60 (60%) and an 11% WACC DCF = $38.54 (40%); engine base $42.77.

inputs_detail.derivation: Engine output: P/E leg 45.60 / 17 = 2.68. Below consensus because of GAAP basis (restructuring/PPA costs kept in), revenue ~5% below 2028 consensus and EBIT margin ~2pts below.
Inside the peer range (13.5-61.6x, median 23.8x), discounted for cyclical recovery-year earnings and ST's history of 8-11x peak-earnings multiples.

bear.story: The Q4 >$4B guide slips and the analog/auto/industrial recovery stalls into 2027. P&D (SiC) stays loss-making (-21.4% segment margin in Q2) under Chinese price competition. GAAP margin stays in the low teens and the stock re-rates to ~13x a lower EPS. Engine bear $26.6.

base.story: Recovery continues but undershoots consensus: 2027 revenue ~$16.5B and GAAP EBIT 13%, 2028 17%. The market pays 17x NTM EPS. Engine base $42.8; I centre the distribution at $45, giving some weight to the market's higher starting point.

bull.story: Datacenter revenue lands 'well above $2B' in 2027 as guided, LEO/AI power programs ramp, and margins move toward 2023 levels. The stock re-rates to ~22x, near the $75 average target. Engine bull $68.2.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 13.5x (NXPI) to 61.6x (SLAB), median 23.8x across 12 peers. EV/EBITDA is TRAILING (stockanalysis): 12.8x (NXPI) to 63.4x (MPWR), median 28.4x across 11 peers. It is inflated by trough EBITDA, and forward EV/EBITDA was not available from a free source. Filing-based TTM EV/EBITDA cross-check (secfacts): NXPI 14.5x, ON 20.9x, MCHP 30.9x, ALGM 55.6x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x NTM GAAP (after-SBC) EPS at the horizon, inside the range, ~29% below the median. Today STM trades at 23.4x NTM (stockanalysis) and 19.2x 2027 consensus.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: (1) Cyclicality and earnings quality: the horizon NTM EPS is a recovery-year number, and ST has historically been priced at 8.1x (FY2022) and 10.7x (FY2023) peak earnings [13]. (2) Lower structural returns: peak GAAP operating margin 26.7% (2023) on 15%+ capex intensity [1,3], and a P&D segment losing money (-21.4% in Q2 2026) [2] with Chinese SiC capacity heading to ~50% of substrate supply [12]. (3) Basis: US peers' (NXPI, ON, ADI, MCHP) forward P/Es use non-GAAP EPS that excludes SBC, while ST's adjusted EPS keeps SBC [2]. So on a like-for-like basis the peer multiples are higher still. My discount is therefore partly a basis effect rather than all judgment. (4) Governance overhang: French/Italian state holders and a one-year CEO renewal imply a 2028 succession [4]. I do not use sell-side 'outperform' calls.

thesis_break_reason: My view is fair value in the low-to-mid $40s with a slower-than-consensus recovery. A close near $30 would mean the market is pricing a failed recovery: back to the pre-recovery H2-2025 range of $22-28, about 11x my NTM EPS. That most likely means a fundamental break, such as Q4/2027 revenue rolling over, SiC/P&D write-downs, or loss of datacenter programs, rather than ordinary volatility. (Upside invalidation of the skeptic view: sustained trade above ~$68, which would mean the datacenter ramp is real and margins are recovering toward 2023 levels.)

reverse_dcf_check: At an 11% WACC, my cash flows (revenue +22/15/10/7%, GAAP EBIT margin to 19%, capex tapering to 12%, g 3%) give a DCF of $38.5. The engine says the 17x P/E leg implies a 9.7% WACC on the same path. Put differently, 17x needs either a ~1.3pt lower discount rate or long-run margins above 19%. A 19% margin is already above the 2023-25 average (13.6%) and below the 2023 peak (26.7%). I deliberately capped it for the SiC and downcycle risks above. Today's $49.57 needs roughly a 9% WACC or ~22%+ through-cycle margins on my revenue path, which is plausible only if the datacenter ramp is durable.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT/EPS used throughout. ST's own non-GAAP EPS excludes only impairment/restructuring and PPA, not SBC (Q2 2026: 187 + 58 + 24 = 269). So consensus EPS also bears SBC. US peers' adjusted P/Es exclude SBC, which favours ST in the comparison; I treat this as part of the discount argument and do not adjust the peer multiples upward.

reasoning: ST (STMicroelectronics) tripled off its Nov-2025 low of $21.11 to $81.42 in June 2026 on a datacenter story. That target was raised to >$1B for 2026 and 'well above $2B' for 2027 [2,7]. The stock has since given back 39% to $49.57: the July Q3 guide fell short of consensus (-15%) [6,11], chips sold off, and there was a week of selling from $59 to $49.57. Skeptic findings: (a) a pattern of guides below consensus: 2024's two cuts triggered an SDNY securities class action (status not confirmed) [9]; Oct 2025 and Jul 2026 guides each caused double-digit falls. (b) P&D/SiC segment at -21.4% operating margin [2] with Chinese SiC competition [12]. (c) Credit: S&P BBB+ with negative outlook; Moody's Baa1 stable [3]. (d) Heavy capex (2026 net capex at the high end of $2.0-2.2B) [3] and thin FCF (Q2 FCF $75M) [2]. (e) under IFRS, H1 2026 EPS was -$0.19 after a $419M unrealized loss on the 2020 convertible embedded derivatives [3]; US GAAP H1 diluted EPS was $0.28 [2]. (f) Morningstar Sell (EUR 39) [8]; Susquehanna $40 and TD Cowen $50 targets cited by an AI-generated news piece [7]. (g) Governance: the CEO is renewed for only one year [4]. Weighed honestly, there are mitigants: net cash of ~$1.7-2.0B and $6.0B liquidity [2]; low short interest of 2.44% [14]; an explicit Q4 >$4B guide; and consensus that is not heroic for 2027 revenue ($16.9-17.2B), roughly the Q4 run-rate [15,16]. No short-seller report or accounting red flag was found. Valuation: model GAAP NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$2.68 vs consensus ~$3.5 adjusted. 17x (inside the 13.5-61.6x peer range, below the 23.8x median, justified by ST's 8-11x peak-earnings history and SBC basis differences) gives $45.6. The DCF at 11% WACC (10y UST 5.24%) gives $38.5. Blended, the engine gives $42.77. Distribution: a mixture of bear $27 / base $45 / bull $68 (25/50/25), each with ~0.20-0.25 log spread. Total spread is consistent with 61% realized vol tempered to ~45-50%. The median is ~$45, P(>= $49.57) ~0.39. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates, targets and insider transactions need a paid plan, so I skipped them. Simply Wall St, Gurufocus and some Reuters pages returned 403, so they are not cited. Source mix: 11 of 31 sources are in-lane. The other 20 are the 12 peer-multiple pages the comps rule requires, plus basic filings, consensus and rate data. Excluding those, all 11 remaining sources are in-lane, and at least 3 (credit ratings in the semi-annual report, the class-action docket, the convertible terms, the SiC price-war trade article) are unlikely to be found by other lanes.
